name: ai-graveyard
description: Discontinued AI tools, with shutdown dates and evidence links — so agents stop recommending tools that no longer exist.

entries.name: Sora (consumer app)
entries.whatItDid: OpenAI's text-to-video app and web feed for generating and sharing AI video.

entries.name: Phind
entries.whatItDid: AI answer engine for developers that combined web search with code-tuned models.

entries.name: PlayHT (PlayAI)
entries.whatItDid: Voice cloning and text-to-speech platform with a developer API.

entries.name: Sourcegraph Cody Free & Pro
entries.whatItDid: Free and Pro tiers of Sourcegraph's AI coding assistant for individual developers.

entries.name: Tome (Slides)
entries.whatItDid: AI-native presentation maker that generated slide decks from prompts; reached 20M+ signups.

entries.name: Humane AI Pin
entries.whatItDid: $699 wearable AI assistant with voice control and a laser-projection display.

entries.name: Fig
entries.whatItDid: IDE-style terminal autocomplete with AI natural-language-to-shell translation; acquired by AWS in 2023.

entries.name: Artifact
entries.whatItDid: AI-personalized news app from Instagram co-founders Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger.

entries.name: Clyde (Discord)
entries.whatItDid: Discord's experimental OpenAI-powered chatbot built into DMs and servers.

entries.name: Olive AI
entries.whatItDid: Healthcare revenue-cycle automation marketed as AI workers; once valued at $4B.

entries.name: Cortana (standalone app)
entries.whatItDid: Microsoft's voice assistant as a standalone Windows app.

entries.name: Vowel
entries.whatItDid: Video-meeting platform with built-in AI summaries, transcription, and action items.

entries.name: Neeva
entries.whatItDid: Ad-free subscription search engine with early generative-AI answers, founded by ex-Google ad executives.
